title: Hall Effect
theory: A conducting strip (thickness $a$, width $b$, length $c$) carries current $I$ via $n$ carriers per volume, charge magnitude $q$, drifting at $v$. **Box counting:** in time $t$, the carriers crossing a section fill a box of volume $(ab)(vt)$ ⇒ $N = nabvt$ ⇒ $I = qnabv$. Apply $B$ perpendicular to the broad face: the magnetic force $qvB$ shovels carriers sideways until the built-up transverse field balances it: $qE = qvB \Rightarrow E = vB$; the Hall voltage spans the width **along the force**: $V_H = Eb = vBb$. Eliminating $v$ measures the carrier density — and the polarity of $V_H$ reveals the carrier **sign**: that is the Hall effect's whole point.
framework: Multiply by the dimension the voltage spans.

parts.title: Carriers crossing a section in time t
parts.parameters:
- Given: strip of thickness $a$, width $b$, length $c$; current $I$ along the length; carrier density $n$, charge magnitude $q$, drift speed $v$; then a field $B$ applied perpendicular to the broad ($b\times c$) face; a steady voltage $V$ appears across the width $b$.
- Find: carriers passing in time $t$; the current; the magnetic force per carrier; the Hall voltage; $n$ in terms of measured quantities.

parts.title: Carrier density from measurements
parts.parameters:
- Given: strip of thickness $a$, width $b$, length $c$; current $I$ along the length; carrier density $n$, charge magnitude $q$, drift speed $v$; then a field $B$ applied perpendicular to the broad ($b\times c$) face; a steady voltage $V$ appears across the width $b$.

parts.conclusion: the length $c$ **never appears** — discard any option containing it on sight. The voltage spans $b$, yet $b$ cancels from the final $n$: run the cancellation once so it's yours forever. Sign bonus: for negative carriers the accumulation side flips — which is how Hall measurements identify electrons vs. holes.
